source: Public free questions (numbers 1 to 10) from the Gulf Nursing Licensure Studio build, branch claude/gulf-crosswalk. Paid questions are never included.

shared.stem: A nurse receives handoff on four patients. Which patient should be assessed first?

options.label: A
options.text: A postoperative patient with incisional pain 7/10 thirty minutes after analgesia.

options.label: B
options.text: A patient with COPD whose SpO2 is 91% on prescribed oxygen and unchanged from baseline.

options.label: C
options.text: A patient 2 hours after extubation with new inspiratory stridor and increasing retractions.

options.label: D
options.text: A patient with an NG tube reporting nausea and 150 mL green drainage in 2 hours.

shared.answerText: A patient 2 hours after extubation with new inspiratory stridor and increasing retractions.
shared.rationale: New stridor after extubation suggests an evolving upper-airway obstruction.
shared.pearl: Treat the earliest unresolved life threat, then reassess from A again.
shared.trap: Do not use ABCDE Priority Framework as a rigid slogan; compare the patient's actual severity, timing, safety, scope, and response.

shared.stem: A patient with pneumonia has SpO2 84%, RR 34/min, and accessory-muscle use. What should the nurse do first?

options.label: A
options.text: Complete a detailed pain assessment before changing the respiratory plan.

options.label: B
options.text: Encourage oral fluids and reassess the respiratory rate in 30 minutes.

options.label: C
options.text: Position the patient upright, apply appropriate oxygen, and rapidly reassess breathing and response.

options.label: D
options.text: Obtain a sputum specimen before starting an intervention that may alter respiratory findings.

shared.answerText: Position the patient upright, apply appropriate oxygen, and rapidly reassess breathing and response.
shared.rationale: The patient has an immediate breathing problem requiring support and reassessment.
shared.pearl: Treat the earliest unresolved life threat, then reassess from A again.
shared.trap: Do not use ABCDE Priority Framework as a rigid slogan; compare the patient's actual severity, timing, safety, scope, and response.

shared.stem: A patient with an upper GI bleed becomes pale and restless; BP falls to 82/48 mmHg and HR rises to 132/min. What should the nurse do first?

options.label: A
options.text: Call for urgent help, support circulation, obtain rapid vascular access as appropriate, and reassess perfusion.

options.label: B
options.text: Ask the patient to rate abdominal pain before initiating other care.

options.label: C
options.text: Administer the scheduled proton-pump inhibitor and recheck blood pressure in one hour.

options.label: D
options.text: Collect a stool specimen for occult blood before contacting the clinical team.

shared.answerText: Call for urgent help, support circulation, obtain rapid vascular access as appropriate, and reassess perfusion.
shared.rationale: Hypotension, tachycardia, pallor, and restlessness with bleeding indicate circulatory instability.
shared.pearl: Treat the earliest unresolved life threat, then reassess from A again.
shared.trap: Do not use ABCDE Priority Framework as a rigid slogan; compare the patient's actual severity, timing, safety, scope, and response.

shared.stem: A patient suddenly becomes difficult to arouse. Airway is patent, SpO2 96%, RR 16/min, and BP 126/74 mmHg. What should the nurse do next?

options.label: A
options.text: Give a rapid IV fluid bolus despite normal perfusion and no evidence of volume loss.

options.label: B
options.text: Delay assessment because oxygenation and blood pressure remain normal.

options.label: C
options.text: Start chest compressions because reduced responsiveness is sufficient to diagnose cardiac arrest.

options.label: D
options.text: Perform a rapid neurologic assessment, check bedside glucose, and escalate the acute change in consciousness.

shared.answerText: Perform a rapid neurologic assessment, check bedside glucose, and escalate the acute change in consciousness.
shared.rationale: With airway, breathing, and circulation adequate, the new neurologic change is the next priority.
shared.pearl: Treat the earliest unresolved life threat, then reassess from A again.
shared.trap: Do not use ABCDE Priority Framework as a rigid slogan; compare the patient's actual severity, timing, safety, scope, and response.

shared.stem: A trauma patient has gurgling respirations and blood in the mouth. Which action is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Open and clear the airway with suction while maintaining appropriate cervical-spine precautions.

options.label: B
options.text: Obtain laboratory specimens before attempting to clear the airway.

options.label: C
options.text: Administer analgesia before performing airway interventions.

options.label: D
options.text: Inspect both legs for deformity before addressing the noisy respirations.

shared.answerText: Open and clear the airway with suction while maintaining appropriate cervical-spine precautions.
shared.rationale: Gurgling with oral blood indicates threatened airway patency.
shared.pearl: Treat the earliest unresolved life threat, then reassess from A again.
shared.trap: Do not use ABCDE Priority Framework as a rigid slogan; compare the patient's actual severity, timing, safety, scope, and response.

shared.stem: A patient with chronic hypercapnic respiratory disease deteriorates and requires oxygen. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Titrate oxygen to the prescribed or clinically appropriate target and reassess work of breathing, mentation, and saturation.

options.label: B
options.text: Withhold oxygen until an arterial blood gas confirms the exact cause.

options.label: C
options.text: Give a rapid crystalloid bolus first because respiratory deterioration implies hypovolemia.

options.label: D
options.text: Set oxygen automatically to achieve 100% saturation regardless of the patient condition.

shared.answerText: Titrate oxygen to the prescribed or clinically appropriate target and reassess work of breathing, mentation, and saturation.
shared.rationale: Oxygen therapy should treat hypoxemia while being individualized and reassessed.
shared.pearl: Treat the earliest unresolved life threat, then reassess from A again.
shared.trap: Do not use ABCDE Priority Framework as a rigid slogan; compare the patient's actual severity, timing, safety, scope, and response.

shared.stem: After supporting a postoperative patient with acute dyspnea, what should the nurse do next?

options.label: A
options.text: Reassess airway and breathing before moving on to circulation and neurologic status.

options.label: B
options.text: Focus only on the original abnormal vital sign rather than reassessing the patient.

options.label: C
options.text: Move directly to discharge planning because the immediate symptom was treated.

options.label: D
options.text: Document the intervention and wait for the next routine observation round.

shared.answerText: Reassess airway and breathing before moving on to circulation and neurologic status.
shared.rationale: After treatment, reassess from the beginning to confirm earlier priorities remain controlled.
shared.pearl: Treat the earliest unresolved life threat, then reassess from A again.
shared.trap: Do not use ABCDE Priority Framework as a rigid slogan; compare the patient's actual severity, timing, safety, scope, and response.

shared.stem: A patient with severe asthma has loud wheezing, then becomes quieter while remaining tachypneic and exhausted. What is the priority interpretation?

options.label: A
options.text: The quieter chest indicates bronchodilator therapy has been effective.

options.label: B
options.text: The patient is ready for discharge teaching because wheezing is no longer prominent.

options.label: C
options.text: The reduced breath sounds may reflect worsening airflow obstruction and impending respiratory failure.

options.label: D
options.text: The change is most consistent with anxiety because the respiratory rate is high.

shared.answerText: The reduced breath sounds may reflect worsening airflow obstruction and impending respiratory failure.
shared.rationale: A quiet chest in severe asthma can represent critically reduced airflow rather than improvement.
shared.pearl: Treat the earliest unresolved life threat, then reassess from A again.
shared.trap: Do not use ABCDE Priority Framework as a rigid slogan; compare the patient's actual severity, timing, safety, scope, and response.

shared.stem: A septic patient is febrile and confused. Which finding requires the most immediate response?

options.label: A
options.text: Poor appetite and generalized weakness for two days.

options.label: B
options.text: BP 78/42 mmHg with cool mottled skin and delayed capillary refill.

options.label: C
options.text: Temperature 39.1 C with chills that began 30 minutes ago.

options.label: D
options.text: WBC 17,000/mm3 reported with morning laboratory results.

shared.answerText: BP 78/42 mmHg with cool mottled skin and delayed capillary refill.
shared.rationale: Profound hypotension with poor perfusion is an immediate circulation threat.
shared.pearl: Treat the earliest unresolved life threat, then reassess from A again.
shared.trap: Do not use ABCDE Priority Framework as a rigid slogan; compare the patient's actual severity, timing, safety, scope, and response.

shared.stem: A patient suddenly becomes dyspneic after central-line removal. Which action should the nurse take first?

options.label: A
options.text: Apply oxygen, position the patient as indicated by the suspected complication, and activate urgent clinical help.

options.label: B
options.text: Obtain a complete medication history before changing the plan.

options.label: C
options.text: Prepare discharge instructions while waiting for review.

options.label: D
options.text: Send a routine message to the team and reassess at the next vital-sign round.

shared.answerText: Apply oxygen, position the patient as indicated by the suspected complication, and activate urgent clinical help.
shared.rationale: Sudden respiratory deterioration requires immediate oxygenation support and escalation while the cause is assessed.
shared.pearl: Treat the earliest unresolved life threat, then reassess from A again.
shared.trap: Do not use ABCDE Priority Framework as a rigid slogan; compare the patient's actual severity, timing, safety, scope, and response.

dubai.stem: A DHA-licensed nurse is allocated a nonurgent procedure that the nurse has never been trained to perform. What is the best response?

options.label: A
options.text: Ask the patient to accept the additional risk.

options.label: B
options.text: Explain the competence gap and arrange a suitably qualified practitioner.

options.label: C
options.text: Proceed while a colleague gives instructions by telephone.

options.label: D
options.text: Perform it because a prescriber has requested it.

dubai.answerText: Explain the competence gap and arrange a suitably qualified practitioner.
dubai.rationale: The request does not establish competence. Arranging qualified help protects the patient without abandoning care.
dubai.pearl: DHA practice: Explain the competence gap and arrange a suitably qualified practitioner.
dubai.trap: Remote instructions do not establish assessed competence.

dubai.stem: A nurse supervising care in a DHA-licensed facility plans to delegate a routine clinical task. Which check is essential?

options.label: A
options.text: Choose the worker who agrees to accept responsibility.

options.label: B
options.text: Confirm that the task fits the worker’s authorized role and demonstrated competence.

options.label: C
options.text: Choose the worker who has the lightest workload.

options.label: D
options.text: Use the worker who has observed the task most often.

dubai.answerText: Confirm that the task fits the worker’s authorized role and demonstrated competence.
dubai.rationale: Willingness and availability do not establish authority or ability. Delegation must fit the person and the task.
dubai.pearl: DHA practice: Confirm that the task fits the worker’s authorized role and demonstrated competence.
dubai.trap: Workload matters only after role and ability are established.

dubai.stem: In Dubai, a nurse delegates an authorized task to a competent team member. Which follow-up is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Remove the task from handover because it was delegated.

options.label: B
options.text: Check the reported outcome and provide supervision matched to the task.

options.label: C
options.text: Review the outcome only if the patient makes a complaint.

options.label: D
options.text: Assume completion because the worker accepted the task.

dubai.answerText: Check the reported outcome and provide supervision matched to the task.
dubai.rationale: Delegation does not end the need for oversight. Outcome review helps identify care that needs adjustment.
dubai.pearl: DHA practice: Check the reported outcome and provide supervision matched to the task.
dubai.trap: Waiting for a complaint misses earlier signs of incomplete care.

dubai.stem: In a DHA-licensed unit, a patient awaiting an elective procedure cannot explain what the procedure involves despite a signed form. What should the nurse do first?

options.label: A
options.text: Ask a relative to confirm that the procedure is acceptable.

options.label: B
options.text: Repeat the procedure name and request another signature.

options.label: C
options.text: Pause preparation and arrange an understandable explanation before consent is confirmed.

options.label: D
options.text: Continue because the signed form is already in the record.

dubai.answerText: Pause preparation and arrange an understandable explanation before consent is confirmed.
dubai.rationale: A signature alone does not show informed agreement. The misunderstanding must be addressed before the elective procedure proceeds.
dubai.pearl: DHA practice: Pause preparation and arrange an understandable explanation before consent is confirmed.
dubai.trap: A form does not resolve the stated misunderstanding.

dubai.stem: A capable adult in Dubai asks to discuss an alternative treatment. A family member prefers the proposed plan. What should the nurse do?

options.label: A
options.text: Support the patient in discussing options with the treating clinician.

options.label: B
options.text: Ask the family to decide which option will be discussed.

options.label: C
options.text: Discourage further questions because a plan is documented.

options.label: D
options.text: Ask the patient to decide without further information.

dubai.answerText: Support the patient in discussing options with the treating clinician.
dubai.rationale: Care should support the patient’s informed participation. Family involvement should not prevent the patient from receiving information.
dubai.pearl: DHA practice: Support the patient in discussing options with the treating clinician.
dubai.trap: Family preference does not displace a capable adult’s voice.

dubai.stem: In a Dubai clinic, a caller requests an adult patient’s test results and claims to be a relative. Permission to disclose has not been established. What is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Give the results if the person knows the patient’s birth date.

options.label: B
options.text: Ask another visitor to confirm the relationship.

options.label: C
options.text: Verify identity and the authority to receive information before disclosure.

options.label: D
options.text: Share only the abnormal results to limit disclosure.

dubai.answerText: Verify identity and the authority to receive information before disclosure.
dubai.rationale: The request alone does not authorize disclosure. Identity and a valid basis for access must both be established.
dubai.pearl: DHA practice: Verify identity and the authority to receive information before disclosure.
dubai.trap: Selected results are still confidential information.

dubai.stem: In a Dubai ward, a stable patient’s sensitive history is being discussed within hearing of unrelated visitors. What is the best action?

options.label: A
options.text: Move the conversation to a private setting with the patient’s agreement.

options.label: B
options.text: Continue quietly while using the patient’s room number.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask visitors to ignore the conversation and continue.

options.label: D
options.text: Omit the patient’s name but discuss the full history.

dubai.answerText: Move the conversation to a private setting with the patient’s agreement.
dubai.rationale: Avoidable exposure of personal information should be reduced. Omitting a name does not make an identifiable bedside conversation private.
dubai.pearl: DHA practice: Move the conversation to a private setting with the patient’s agreement.
dubai.trap: Room context can still identify the patient.

dubai.stem: A stable patient in a DHA-licensed unit requests a same-gender practitioner for an intimate examination. What is the best initial response?

options.label: A
options.text: Ask a family member to persuade the patient to withdraw it.

options.label: B
options.text: Cancel all planned care until a same-gender team is available.

options.label: C
options.text: Explore the preference and arrange suitable care where feasible without delaying urgent needs.

options.label: D
options.text: Assume the request applies to every future procedure.

dubai.answerText: Explore the preference and arrange suitable care where feasible without delaying urgent needs.
dubai.rationale: Preferences should be discussed individually and respected where feasible. The nurse must also account for the urgency of care.
dubai.pearl: DHA practice: Explore the preference and arrange suitable care where feasible without delaying urgent needs.
dubai.trap: An individual preference must not be generalized without discussion.

dubai.stem: After administering prescribed analgesia in Dubai, which record best supports safe continuing care?

options.label: A
options.text: Record that all routine care was completed during the shift.

options.label: B
options.text: Record the medicine only if pain remains severe.

options.label: C
options.text: Record the intended response before reassessment occurs.

options.label: D
options.text: Record the assessment, medicine given, time, and reassessed response.

dubai.answerText: Record the assessment, medicine given, time, and reassessed response.
dubai.rationale: The record should show what was done and how the patient responded. Intended outcomes must not be recorded as observed facts.
dubai.pearl: DHA practice: Record the assessment, medicine given, time, and reassessed response.
dubai.trap: A broad completion statement omits important clinical details.

dubai.stem: A patient in Dubai needs more oxygen than earlier in the shift. Which handover is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: List completed routine tasks before ending the handover.

options.label: B
options.text: Describe the change, current observations, actions taken, and required follow-up.

options.label: C
options.text: Describe the admission diagnosis and leave changes in the chart.

options.label: D
options.text: Report that the patient is comfortable without mentioning oxygen.

dubai.answerText: Describe the change, current observations, actions taken, and required follow-up.
dubai.rationale: A new oxygen requirement is a relevant change in condition. The receiving team needs the current situation and outstanding actions.
dubai.pearl: DHA practice: Describe the change, current observations, actions taken, and required follow-up.
dubai.trap: The chart does not replace communication of a significant change.

saudi.intro: 200 multiple-choice questions in two blocks of 100, each 120 minutes, with a scheduled break. SCFHS reports a scaled score from 200 to 800; 500 is the pass mark.
saudi.retake: SCFHS sources differ: the applicant guide describes up to four attempts a year, while the SCFHS dates page describes three attempts in an initial cycle with renewal provisions after a year. This is not a lifetime maximum. Confirm with SCFHS before relying on either.

qatar.fullName: Qatar Registered General Nurse Qualifying Examination
qatar.regulator: Department of Healthcare Professions (DHP), Ministry of Public Health

tiles.n: An older DHP document says 3½ hours

qatar.intro: 150 multiple-choice questions. The current DHP exam page says 3 hours; an older DHP blueprint document says 3½ hours, so check the time on your booking confirmation.
qatar.retake: DHP policy (v04) and the qualifying-examination page describe five attempts. A three-attempt line sits under physician specialties and does not clearly apply to nurses. Effective dates are not stated; not confirmed in writing by DHP.

tiles.n: Result shown as pass or fail

dubai.intro: 150 multiple-choice questions in 3 hours. The 3 hours includes registration and a short introduction, so your answering time is a little less.
dubai.retake: General DHA licensing rules apply: three attempts across UAE authorities, a fourth only with permission, and a two-year block after the third failure before new attempts. Sources differ on details; confirm with DHA.

abudhabi.fullName: Abu Dhabi Department of Health Registered Nurse

tiles.n: DOH reports pass or fail only
A final attempt may be approved

abudhabi.intro: 150 multiple-choice questions in 3 hours (DOH nursing licensing circular, 2024). DOH reports a pass or fail result and does not publish its pass mark.
abudhabi.retake: UAE-wide rules allow three attempts across authorities, with a possible final attempt subject to approval. Confirm with DOH.

disclaimer: Original practice material, not official exam questions. Not endorsed by SCFHS, DHP, DHA or DOH.
